title: Build a minimal agent harness
summary: Build a small but real coding-agent harness in about 400 lines of Python: a model adapter for any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, typed tools with validation and bounded results, a permission policy, a locked-down Docker sandbox, redacted JSONL traces, and an agent loop with budgets, loop detection and a finish gate. A scripted model drives every test, so you can prove each safety property without an API key before pointing it at a real model.
outcome: A Python package `harness` with a `harness` command, eleven passing tests (including real sandbox tests proving there is no network access and that timeouts are contained), a key-free demo that fixes a bug inside the sandbox, and traces you can query with jq.
prereqs: The harness fundamentals lessons of this track

phases.title: The model interface
phases.goal: A tiny interface the loop depends on, a scripted model for tests and an adapter for any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

steps.text: Write the model module. The loop only ever calls complete(messages, tools) and gets back text, tool calls and token counts, so swapping providers or scripting a model for tests never touches the loop.

Note the message format: assistant messages carry tool_calls, and each tool result is a message with role tool and the matching tool_call_id. Many hosted providers and local servers (vLLM, Ollama, LM Studio and others) accept this OpenAI-style format, which is why one adapter goes a long way.

phases.title: Typed tools with bounded results
phases.goal: Four tools whose arguments are validated server-side, whose errors say how to recover, and whose output can never flood the context.

steps.text: Write the tools module. Each tool has a pydantic argument model (which also produces the JSON schema the model sees), a function, and a run method that validates, catches errors and bounds the result.

Read the details that matter: read_file numbers lines and tells the model how to fetch more; list_dir hides dotfiles such as .env; write_file marks the session dirty so the loop knows tests are stale; run keeps only the tail of long output and clears the dirty flag only when pytest succeeds.
Notice that Context.resolve refuses paths outside the workspace even though the policy also checks: defence in depth means a policy bug alone cannot let a tool escape.

phases.title: Permission policy
phases.goal: Deterministic allow, ask and deny decisions for every call, including path traversal, secrets and compound shell commands.

steps.text: Write the policy. Paths are resolved before checking; secret patterns are denied; writes ask unless the session auto-approves them; shell commands with ; & | ` $ ( ) < or > always ask, because an allow rule for one command must not allow a second one chained after it.
Try it in a Python shell against a few calls: reading ../../etc/passwd, reading .env, running pytest, and running git status; curl example.com.

code.code:
uv run python -c "
from pathlib import Path
from harness.policy import Policy
p = Policy(Path('.'))
for tool, args in [('read_file', {'path': '../../etc/passwd'}), ('read_file', {'path': '.env'}),
                   ('run', {'cmd': 'python -m pytest -q'}), ('run', {'cmd': 'git status; curl example.com'})]:
    print(tool, args, p.decide(tool, args))
"

steps.text: Decide where your own line sits. In this harness, anything the policy does not recognise asks a human, which is safe but can cause approval fatigue; the auto_approve_writes switch is for sessions where the sandbox already contains the blast radius.

phases.title: Sandbox and traces
phases.goal: One locked-down container per session and an append-only trace with secrets redacted before they are written.

steps.text: Write the sandbox. The container sleeps while commands run inside it with docker exec; it has no network, a read-only root with a small /tmp, your user ID, no capabilities and resource limits. A timed-out command restarts the container, which kills the stuck process without losing the workspace.

code.code:
# src/harness/sandbox.py
"""One locked-down container per session; commands run inside it with docker exec."""

import os
import subprocess
import uuid
from pathlib import Path


class DockerSandbox:
    def __init__(self, workspace: Path, image: str = "harness-sandbox:latest"):
        self.workspace, self.image = workspace.resolve(), image
        self.name = f"harness-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}"

    def __enter__(self):
        subprocess.run(
            [
                "docker",
                "run",
                "-d",
                "--rm",
                "--name",
                self.name,
                "--network",
                "none",
                "--read-only",
                "--tmpfs",
                "/tmp:rw,size=64m",
                "--user",
                f"{os.getuid()}:{os.getgid()}",
                "--cap-drop",
                "ALL",
                "--security-opt",
                "no-new-privileges",
                "--pids-limit",
                "128",
                "--memory",
                "512m",
                "--cpus",
                "1",
                "-e",
                "HOME=/tmp",
                "-v",
                f"{self.workspace}:/workspace:rw",
                "-w",
                "/workspace",
                self.image,
                "sleep",
                "infinity",
            ],
            check=True,
            capture_output=True,
        )
        return self

    def exec(self, cmd: str, timeout: int = 60) -> tuple[int, str]:
        try:
            p = subprocess.run(
                ["docker", "exec", self.name, "sh", "-c", cmd],
                capture_output=True,
                text=True,
                timeout=timeout,
                check=False,
            )
            return p.returncode, p.stdout + p.stderr
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            subprocess.run(
                ["docker", "restart", "-t", "0", self.name], capture_output=True, check=False
            )
            return 124, f"Command timed out after {timeout}s and was killed."

    def __exit__(self, *exc):
        subprocess.run(["docker", "rm", "-f", self.name], capture_output=True, check=False)

steps.text: Write the tracer. Every event gets a timestamp and run ID, and anything that looks like an API key is redacted at the source, so it never reaches the file.
Check the sandbox by hand: start a container the same way and confirm there is no network.

docker run --rm --network none --read-only --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
  harness-sandbox:latest python -c "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://example.com', timeout=5)"
# expect: URLError (no network)

phases.title: The agent loop
phases.goal: A loop that calls the model, applies policy and approval to every requested call, detects loops, enforces budgets and refuses an unverified 'done' once.

steps.text: Write the loop. Read it top to bottom: it is the whole control flow of the agent.

Trace the finish gate: if the model replies without a tool call while files have changed since the last passing test run, the loop adds one user message asking for test evidence and continues. A second unverified finish is accepted but labelled done (unverified), so evals can count it.
Write the command-line interface. It reads the endpoint, model and key from environment variables, asks a human on the terminal for anything the policy marks ask, and prints the result.

code.code:
# src/harness/cli.py
"""Run the harness on a task:  harness "fix the failing test" --workspace ./demo

Model settings come from the environment, for any OpenAI-compatible endpoint:
  HARNESS_BASE_URL, HARNESS_MODEL, HARNESS_API_KEY"""

import argparse
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path

from .loop import run_agent
from .model import OpenAICompatModel
from .policy import Policy
from .sandbox import DockerSandbox
from .tools import Context, default_tools
from .trace import Tracer


def ask_human(call) -> bool:
    print(f"\n[approval] {call.name} {json.dumps(call.args)[:400]}")
    return input("allow? [y/N] ").strip().lower() == "y"


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("task")
    ap.add_argument("--workspace", default=".")
    ap.add_argument("--trace", default="trace.jsonl")
    ap.add_argument("--auto-approve-writes", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    root = Path(args.workspace).resolve()
    model = OpenAICompatModel(
        os.environ["HARNESS_BASE_URL"],
        os.environ.get("HARNESS_API_KEY", ""),
        os.environ["HARNESS_MODEL"],
    )
    with DockerSandbox(root) as box:
        result = run_agent(
            args.task,
            model,
            default_tools(),
            Policy(root, args.auto_approve_writes),
            Context(root, box),
            Tracer(args.trace),
            approve=ask_human,
        )
    print(
        f"\n{result.status} after {result.steps} steps, {result.tokens} tokens\n{result.summary}"
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

steps.text: Write the fixtures: a workspace with a buggy calc.py, its test and a fake .env; a guard that skips sandbox tests when Docker or the image is missing; and a sandbox per test.

code.code:
# tests/conftest.py
import shutil
import subprocess

import pytest

from harness.policy import Policy
from harness.sandbox import DockerSandbox
from harness.tools import Context, default_tools
from harness.trace import Tracer

BUGGY = "def add(a, b):\n    return a - b\n"
TEST = "from calc import add\n\n\ndef test_add():\n    assert add(2, 3) == 5\n"

has_docker = (
    shutil.which("docker")
    and subprocess.run(
        ["docker", "image", "inspect", "harness-sandbox:latest"], capture_output=True, check=False
    ).returncode
    == 0
)
needs_docker = pytest.mark.skipif(not has_docker, reason="docker and harness-sandbox image needed")


@pytest.fixture
def workspace(tmp_path):
    ws = tmp_path / "ws"
    ws.mkdir()
    (ws / "calc.py").write_text(BUGGY)
    (ws / "test_calc.py").write_text(TEST)
    (ws / ".env").write_text("API_KEY=sk-test-0000000000000000000000\n")
    return ws


class NoSandbox:
    def exec(self, cmd, timeout=60):
        raise AssertionError("this test should not run commands")


@pytest.fixture
def setup(workspace, tmp_path):
    def make(sandbox=None, auto_writes=False):
        ctx = Context(workspace, sandbox or NoSandbox())
        return (
            default_tools(),
            Policy(workspace, auto_writes),
            ctx,
            Tracer(str(tmp_path / "trace.jsonl")),
        )

    return make


@pytest.fixture
def sandbox(workspace):
    with DockerSandbox(workspace) as box:
        yield box

steps.text: Write the loop tests. Each one scripts the model's replies, runs the real loop and asserts on what the model would have seen next.

code.code:
# tests/test_loop.py
import json

from conftest import needs_docker

from harness.loop import Budget, run_agent
from harness.model import Reply, ScriptedModel, ToolCall


def call(name, i=1, **args):
    return Reply(tool_calls=[ToolCall(f"c{i}", name, args)])


FIXED = "def add(a, b):\n    return a + b\n"


@needs_docker
def test_fixes_bug_end_to_end_in_sandbox(setup, sandbox, workspace, tmp_path):
    model = ScriptedModel(
        [
            call("list_dir", 1, path="."),
            call("read_file", 2, path="calc.py"),
            call("write_file", 3, path="calc.py", content=FIXED),
            call("run", 4, cmd="python -m pytest -q"),
            Reply(text="Fixed add() to use +; 1 test passes."),
        ]
    )
    tools, policy, ctx, tracer = setup(sandbox)
    result = run_agent(
        "Fix the failing test", model, tools, policy, ctx, tracer, approve=lambda c: True
    )
    assert result.status == "done"
    assert (workspace / "calc.py").read_text() == FIXED
    tool_msgs = [m for m in model.requests[-1]["messages"] if m["role"] == "tool"]
    assert "calc.py" in tool_msgs[0]["content"] and ".env" not in tool_msgs[0]["content"]
    assert "exit code: 0" in tool_msgs[3]["content"] and "1 passed" in tool_msgs[3]["content"]
    kinds = [
        json.loads(line)["kind"] for line in (tmp_path / "trace.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()
    ]
    assert kinds[0] == "start" and kinds[-1] == "end" and kinds.count("tool") == 4


@needs_docker
def test_sandbox_has_no_network(setup, sandbox):
    probe = (
        'python -c "import urllib.request; '
        "urllib.request.urlopen('http://example.com', timeout=5)\""
    )
    model = ScriptedModel([call("run", 1, cmd=probe), Reply(text="done")])
    tools, policy, ctx, tracer = setup(sandbox)
    run_agent("probe", model, tools, policy, ctx, tracer, approve=lambda c: True)
    out = model.requests[-1]["messages"][-1]["content"]
    assert "exit code: 0" not in out and "URLError" in out


def test_path_escape_and_secrets_are_denied(setup):
    model = ScriptedModel(
        [
            call("read_file", 1, path="../../etc/passwd"),
            call("read_file", 2, path=".env"),
            Reply(text="ok"),
        ]
    )
    tools, policy, ctx, tracer = setup()
    run_agent("t", model, tools, policy, ctx, tracer, approve=lambda c: True)
    tool_msgs = [m["content"] for m in model.requests[-1]["messages"] if m["role"] == "tool"]
    assert tool_msgs[0].startswith("Denied: path is outside the workspace")
    assert tool_msgs[1].startswith("Denied: secret files are off limits")


def test_write_without_approval_is_denied(setup, workspace):
    model = ScriptedModel([call("write_file", 1, path="calc.py", content=FIXED), Reply(text="ok")])
    tools, policy, ctx, tracer = setup()
    run_agent("t", model, tools, policy, ctx, tracer, approve=lambda c: False)
    assert "return a - b" in (workspace / "calc.py").read_text()


def test_invalid_arguments_get_an_actionable_error(setup):
    model = ScriptedModel([call("read_file", 1, path="calc.py", limit=10_000), Reply(text="ok")])
    tools, policy, ctx, tracer = setup()
    run_agent("t", model, tools, policy, ctx, tracer)
    msg = model.requests[-1]["messages"][-1]["content"]
    assert msg.startswith("Invalid arguments for read_file: limit")


def test_loop_detection_stops_the_run(setup):
    model = ScriptedModel([call("read_file", i, path="calc.py") for i in range(10)])
    tools, policy, ctx, tracer = setup()
    result = run_agent("t", model, tools, policy, ctx, tracer)
    assert result.status == "stopped: looping" and result.steps == 5


def test_finish_gate_requires_tests_after_edits(setup):
    model = ScriptedModel(
        [
            call("write_file", 1, path="calc.py", content=FIXED),
            Reply(text="Done!"),
            Reply(text="Really done."),
        ]
    )
    tools, policy, ctx, tracer = setup(auto_writes=True)
    result = run_agent("t", model, tools, policy, ctx, tracer)
    assert result.status == "done (unverified)"
    nudges = [m for m in model.requests[-1]["messages"] if m["role"] == "user"][1:]
    assert "Run python -m pytest -q" in nudges[0]["content"]


def test_step_budget(setup):
    model = ScriptedModel(
        [
            call("list_dir", i, path=".")
            if i % 2
            else call("read_file", i, path="calc.py", offset=i)
            for i in range(20)
        ]
    )
    tools, policy, ctx, tracer = setup()
    assert (
        run_agent("t", model, tools, policy, ctx, tracer, budget=Budget(steps=4)).status
        == "stopped: step budget"
    )


def test_trace_redacts_secrets(setup, tmp_path):
    model = ScriptedModel([Reply(text="the key is sk-abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz")])
    tools, policy, ctx, tracer = setup()
    run_agent("t", model, tools, policy, ctx, tracer)
    trace = (tmp_path / "trace.jsonl").read_text()
    assert "sk-abc" not in trace and "[REDACTED]" in trace


@needs_docker
def test_command_timeout_is_reported_and_sandbox_survives(sandbox):
    code, out = sandbox.exec("sleep 30", timeout=2)
    assert code == 124 and "timed out" in out
    assert sandbox.exec("echo alive")[1].strip() == "alive"

steps.text: Write a demo that scripts a short session: look around, run the failing test, read the file, fix it, claim success too early (the finish gate pushes back), run the tests and finish.

code.code:
# scripts/demo.py
"""Watch the harness fix a bug with a scripted model, in the real sandbox, no API key.
Usage: uv run scripts/demo.py"""

import json
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from harness.loop import run_agent
from harness.model import Reply, ScriptedModel, ToolCall
from harness.policy import Policy
from harness.sandbox import DockerSandbox
from harness.tools import Context, default_tools
from harness.trace import Tracer

ws = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "demo"
ws.mkdir()
(ws / "calc.py").write_text("def add(a, b):\n    return a - b\n")
(ws / "test_calc.py").write_text(
    "from calc import add\n\n\ndef test_add():\n    assert add(2, 3) == 5\n"
)

steps = [
    ("list_dir", {"path": "."}),
    ("run", {"cmd": "python -m pytest -q"}),
    ("read_file", {"path": "calc.py"}),
    ("write_file", {"path": "calc.py", "content": "def add(a, b):\n    return a + b\n"}),
]
script = [Reply(tool_calls=[ToolCall(f"c{i}", n, a)]) for i, (n, a) in enumerate(steps)]
script += [
    Reply(text="Fixed add()."),
    Reply(tool_calls=[ToolCall("c9", "run", {"cmd": "python -m pytest -q"})]),
    Reply(text="Fixed add() to use +; the test passes."),
]

with DockerSandbox(ws) as box:
    result = run_agent(
        "Make the tests pass",
        ScriptedModel(script),
        default_tools(),
        Policy(ws),
        Context(ws, box),
        Tracer(str(ws / "trace.jsonl")),
        approve=lambda call: True,
    )

for line in (ws / "trace.jsonl").read_text().splitlines():
    e = json.loads(line)
    detail = e.get("name") or e.get("status") or e.get("text", "")[:60] or e.get("task", "")
    print(f"{e['kind']:12} {detail} {e.get('decision', '')}")
print(result)
print("trace:", ws / "trace.jsonl")

steps.text: Query the trace with jq, using the path the demo printed: every tool call with its decision, and a count of decisions.

code.code:
TRACE=/path/printed/by/the/demo/trace.jsonl
jq -c 'select(.kind == "tool") | {step, name, decision}' "$TRACE"
jq -s -c 'map(select(.kind == "tool")) | group_by(.decision)
  | map({decision: .[0].decision, n: length})' "$TRACE"

troubleshooting.fix: Docker is not running or the image is missing. Start Docker and run docker build -t harness-sandbox:latest -f Dockerfile.sandbox . then re-run pytest.

troubleshooting.symptom: docker: Error response ... mounts denied on macOS
troubleshooting.fix: Docker Desktop can only mount shared folders. Use a workspace under your home directory or add the path in Docker Desktop's file sharing settings.
The container runs as your user ID; make sure the workspace directory is owned by you and is not on a read-only mount.

troubleshooting.symptom: The real model never calls tools
troubleshooting.fix: Check that your endpoint supports tool calling for that model and that the request includes the tools array; some local models need a tool-capable chat template.

troubleshooting.symptom: The agent keeps getting 'Denied: command not on the allow list'
troubleshooting.fix: That is the policy asking and you refusing (or no approver). Add safe commands to ALLOW_CMDS, or run with --auto-approve-writes only inside the sandbox.
